scams.name: The Lake Bled Unlicensed Pletna 'Private' Charter
scams.tldr: He says €25 per person, that the official boats have a queue, that his is 'the same boat, just private.' The wooden hull looks identical to the Pletna boats you've seen photos of.
scams.description: He says €25 per person, that the official boats have a queue, that his is 'the same boat, just private.' The wooden hull looks identical to the Pletna boats you've seen photos of. He promises to wait at the island and bring you back. You climb in because the dragging-yourself-around-the-lake plan suddenly feels heavier than the convenience of stepping aboard, and after you arrive, the price is €40 per person on the way back instead of the €25 quoted out.
scams.avoidance: Use only official Pletna boats from the designated stations around the lake. The fixed rate is €15 round trip per person — no negotiation needed. Or rent a rowing boat for €20/hour and row yourself (it's only 400m). The walk around the lake is 6km and beautiful — you don't need a boat at all.
scams.location: Lake Bled shoreline near Mlino, Velika Zaka, the rowing-club beach by the cycle path, the photo viewpoint paths near the Mala Osojnica viewpoint trailhead

scams.name: The Slovenia Highway-Vignette Missing-Sticker Fine
scams.tldr: A few days later — sometimes weeks later — your rental-car company forwards you a fine of €300–800 from DARS (the Slovenian motorway authority) plus a €30–50 administrative fee from the rental company for handling the paperwork.
scams.description: A few days later — sometimes weeks later — your rental-car company forwards you a fine of €300–800 from DARS (the Slovenian motorway authority) plus a €30–50 administrative fee from the rental company for handling the paperwork. The reason: you drove a Slovenian motorway without an active e-vignette, and the camera over the carriageway recorded your number plate.
scams.avoidance: Buy the e-vignette online at evinjeta.dars.si before entering Slovenia. It's €15 for a 7-day vignette, €30 for a month. Check if your rental car already has one — ask the rental company explicitly. Police enforcement is active, especially on the highway from Austria to Bled.
scams.location: Slovenian motorways (avtocesta) — A1, A2, the Karawanken Tunnel approach from Austria, the H4 and H3 expressways, the toll gantries on the Ljubljana–Bled corridor
